ประมาณ 200 ปีก่อน; จดทะเบียนวัด พ.ศ. 243: About 200 years ago; registered as a temple in 1893 (2436 BE)
หลักฐานของสำนักงานนโยบายและแผนทรัพยากรธร: Evidence from the Samnakngan Nayobai Lae Phaen Sapphayakon Thammachat Lae Singwaetlom (Office of Natural Resources and Environmental Policy and Planning) states that Wat Khiri Khet began as a residence for forest monks to practice asceticism, and was about 200 years old when the database was compiled. A more precise founding year cannot be confirmed yet. The local name 'Wat Lum' reflects its low-lying terrain in the old market area.
แหล่งข้อมูลท้องถิ่นอีกชุดระบุว่าวัดสร้าง: Another set of local sources states that the temple was built or registered on 15 May 1893 (2436 BE) and later used the name Wat Phrathat Khiri Khet, affiliated with the Maha Nikaya sect. Inside, there is an ancient pagoda base with a large banyan tree growing on it, and Buddha relics serve as the center of faith.
ในภาพเมืองตะกั่วป่ายุคเหมืองแร่และการค้า: In the picture of Takua Pa during the mining and maritime trade era, the temple was located near the old market and the community where Hokkien Chinese and miners settled. However, verifiable sources do not state whether this temple was built by a governor or any specific individual, and there is no direct evidence linking the founders to any Chinese group. Therefore, it is safer to say that the temple served as a religious site and spiritual anchor for the old town community, rather than guessing its founder.
พ.ศ. 2462·2563; เหตุการณ์บางช่วงยังไม่ทร: 1919 (2462 BE) · 2020 (2563 BE); some events do not have a known year
หมุดหมายที่ยืนยันได้คือวัดได้รับพระราชวิ: A verifiable milestone is that the temple received royal boundary demarcation (Wisungkhamasima) on 25 August 1919 (2462 BE), indicating that it had advanced from a meditation space to a fully recognized temple status. Meanwhile, the community still called it 'Wat Lum' or 'Wat Talat Tai'.
ระหว่างทาง รอยพระพุทธบาทจำลองซึ่งสร้างโด: Along the way, a replica of the Buddha's footprint, built by Upasika Kui Limsakun and the Takua Pa Buddhist congregation, was once enshrined on Khao Phrabat before being moved for storage at Wat Senanut Rangsan, and then eventually enshrined in the ordination hall of Wat Phrathat Khiri Khet, according to local data. This allowed the temple to also serve as a repository for the town's symbols of faith.
เอกสารเทศบาลช่วง พ.ศ. 2563 บันทึกว่าวัดม: Thesaban (Municipality) documents around 2020 (2563 BE) recorded that the temple had an ancient ordination hall alongside a new one, a replica of the Buddha's footprint, Pho Than Kaen Rak, and a jade Buddha image. It also noted the construction of a relic pagoda on the Buddha footprint hill and the organization of a Buddha relic procession on Makha Bucha Day. However, no evidence has yet been found to confirm the years of specific restorations, periods of abandonment, registration as an ancient monument, or damage from the 2004 (2547 BE) tsunami.
ข้อมูลล่าสุดที่ตรวจสอบได้แสดงว่าวัดพระธา: The latest verifiable information shows that Wat Phrathat Khiri Khet is still a private Maha Nikaya temple and is listed among the religious sites of Thesaban Mueang Takua Pa (Takua Pa Town Municipality). Today, people still come to pay respects to the Buddha relics, the replica of the Buddha's footprint, Pho Than Kaen Rak, and the jade Buddha image, with both the old and new ordination halls coexisting in the area.

The holy relics were placed on a royal chariot, paraded around Takua Pa old town, and circumambulated around the vihara three times. This event reflects that the temple remains a center of faith and community activity, not just an old building.

หลักฐานที่ระบุปีสร้างอย่างชัดเจนในเวลานี: The clearest evidence specifying a construction year at this time is for the temple's small ordination hall, built in 1970 (2513 BE) by Mrs. Huatbi. As for the year the entire temple complex began construction and the reason for choosing the site, there are no confirming documents yet. Therefore, one should not recount history beyond the available evidence.
วัดแห่งนี้เกิดขึ้นในช่วงปลายยุคที่ตะกั่ว: This temple emerged during the late era when Takua Pa still had shared memories with tin mining. The town has roots as a port community with trade exchanges among people of many nationalities. Later, the tin mining economy and the Chinese community played a significant role. However, no evidence has yet been found that the builders of the ordination hall or Wat Khuan Tham were directly connected to the governor, the mines, or the Hokkien Chinese group.
สิ่งที่พอเห็นบทบาทของสถานที่ได้คือการเป็: What can be seen of the site's role is its function as a community religious site, with the ordination hall serving as a center for rituals and local art. Inside is a bas-relief stone Buddha image, behind it is a character inscription, and the boundary markers (sema) around the ordination hall are shaped as Buddha images in various postures.

Meanwhile, the central religious property register of the Samnakngan Phraphutthasatsana Haeng Chat (National Office of Buddhism) lists 'Wat Khuan Tham (abandoned)' in Takua Pa district. Thus, it can only be confirmed that the temple is recorded as abandoned in government databases; it is unknown when it became abandoned or for what reason.
เมืองตะกั่วป่าเองเปลี่ยนผ่านจากเมืองท่าแ: Takua Pa town itself transitioned from a port and mining town. As tin mining operations gradually ceased, economic liveliness decreased, and the old town shifted to being valued as a community heritage. This context helps explain the backdrop of the town's transition, but there is still no direct evidence linking Wat Khuan Tham to the impact of the mine closures.
